calls.reason: Anthropic's posted prices and Fradkin's observed price differences do not establish sustainable premiums or their disappearance. Neither links long-term pricing viability to reliability.

Cottier documents expensive training, but Oviedo estimates much lower inference energy than common estimates, and McFadyen finds performance gains from added compute. This does not settle the broad inefficiency claim.

NBER documents entry and falling prices, while Rhodium reports strong API gross margins and weaker company economics. CAISI finds a capability gap; together these leave the claimed replication-to-low-margin link unclear.
